newsitem.title: GERMANY: U.S. closely watching Albania turmoil - Cohen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. closely watching Albania turmoil - Cohen.

text.p: The United States is watching the turmoil in Albania closely but its armed forces have not been asked to evacuate more than 1,000 Americans living in the Balkan country, U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen said on Wednesday.

"As of this time, there are are no military plans that have either been instituted or any need to call upon the U.S. military at this time," Cohen said in response to questions at a news conference during a visit to Germany.
"So we are watching it," Cohen said. "To the extent that some action is called for in the future, obviously then we will make preparations. But there has been no such call at this time."
Unrest in the former hardline communist country has intensified in recent days following the collapse of pyramid investment schemes in which many people had invested their life savings.

U.S. Army General George Joulwan, commander of American as well as NATO military forces in Europe, told reporters at the news conference that the United States already had warships in the region and was in contact with U.S. Ambassador Marisa Lino in Tirana.
"We are in communication with the ambassador," he said. "We are watching it very closely, but in recent conversations with our ambassador, right now there is no need for action."

U.S. State Department spokesman Nick Burns said in Washington earlier in the week that there were believed to be about 1,600 American citizens in Albania, most of them in the northern part of thecountry and away from violence in the south.
But the State Department this week warned Americans who were thinking of travelling to the country not to do so because of possible danger from political instability.
